issue.title: routing: a plugin's Run-lifetime expiry rests the account for a minute although the account is fine
issue.body:
When a plugin's stream ends with Cursor's native Run expiry (`native Run lifetime expired: the Run timed out; retry your request`, Cursor plugin 0.2.37, magpie-community/plugins#616), routing records the try as `fail: other` and holds the account back for a minute. The account did nothing wrong: the Run's 15-minute lifetime is per request, and the next request on the same account works.

Seen while fixing #4419 / plugins#616 (v0.1.2663). Expected: a lifetime or timeout ending that the plugin marks retryable is not counted against the account — retry it, without resting the account.

Not tried with a real Cursor account.

comments.body:
Fixed on branch [fix/4829-plugin-run-lifetime-no-rest](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4829-plugin-run-lifetime-no-rest) (head `49786b5e0`, on main `8abdf53a8`).

**Root cause**: the plugin's lifetime error reached `failure()` as none of the known kinds. Cursor 0.2.37 ends an expired Run as a contract failure "the gateway can retry or fail over" — `native Run lifetime expired: the Run timed out; retry your request`, as an SSE `error` event (read as 502; its 410 before the stream). `cutWords` knows the plugins' text-form-call cuts (#2873) but not the Run deadline, so the try was told `fail: other`: before any of the answer was sent the gateway failed over to the next member instead of re-asking, and after part of the answer went by — the reporter's case — the break-off path (`lateRests` → `restAfter`'s default branch) counted the failure and rested the account a minute, although the Run's lifetime is per request and the next request on the same account starts a fresh Run and works.

**Fix**: `runLifeWords` (`(?i)native run lifetime expired` — the plugin's contract phrase; the bare pre-0.2.37 wording is covered by the prefix) joins `cutWords` in returning `failCut`: the request is asked again (the same seat once, then the next member), nobody rests, no failure is counted; mid-answer the agent keeps the plugin's words and the account still answers the next request. The plugin's other endings (a Run gone quiet, a cancelled request) and a vendor's own timeout words keep their lanes — the match is the contract's own words, not a generic "timed out", so every vendor's timeout stays where it was.

**Verification** (linux/amd64, go1.27.3, `nogui`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New `TestPluginRunLife*` (retry / mid-answer / other errors), on clean main | 3 red: failover instead of re-asking; mid-answer `Fail: other` + a rest; `failure()` = other |
| Same tests at this tree | ok |
| Product change out of `failure()` by hand | red again |
| `go test ./internal/gateway -tags nogui -count=1` | only main's environment reds (claude client cache, codex client version, marshalRaw vs encoding/json, WSL loopback — the same five on unmodified main; the codex one is order-flaky and passes alone) |
| gofmt -l; linux+windows `go vet`; build | clean / ok |

**Not tried**: a real Cursor account reaching the deadline — the wording is read from the plugin's contract (plugins#616, 3f615ea) and its tests, not from a live Run.
